Ernest Hemingway, The Sun Also Rises.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/ernest-hemingway/the-sun-also-rises

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Ernest Hemingway, the author, died 1961 (Wikidata Q23434, P570 = 1961-07-02).

First publication of the text used: 1926 (SE colophon: 'The Sun Also Rises was published in 1926 by Ernest Hemingway.'). Wikipedia: first published in the United States in October 1926 by Charles Scribner's Sons; the London edition, titled Fiesta, followed in 1927 by Jonathan Cape.

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the edition states the text is in the United States public domain (statement quoted below), and the text was first published in the United States in 1926, before 1931.
- Country of origin (United States): the text was first published in the United States, before 1931, so the US rule settles the country of origin whatever the death year. Hemingway died in 1961, and that date does not change the result.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."

Sources of these facts:
- SE colophon: published 1926 by Ernest Hemingway.
- Wikipedia, The Sun Also Rises: first published in the United States in October 1926 by Charles Scribner's Sons; London edition as Fiesta in 1927 by Jonathan Cape. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sun_Also_Rises
